---
title: "Diversify Your Identity"
date: 2026-11-26
tags: [identity, uncertainty]
---

Under uncertainty, diversification is rational. Success often requires concentrated effort. Can I concentrate effort while diversifying identity?

It occurred to me that I watch more films, across a wider range, than some self-proclaimed movie buffs. Yet I do not derive the same pride from it.

Identification adds a form of gratification beyond the activity itself.

A casual moviegoer becomes a discerning cinephile. A coffee drinker becomes a coffee connoisseur. The activities change less than one's relationship with them.

Much of my identity comes from my intellectual and professional pursuits. This makes my sense of self unnecessarily fragile. A single variable explains too much of its variance.

What if I could concentrate effort along one axis while deriving satisfaction from several?

There is a risk of going too far. I could turn photography, something I enjoy, into another axis along which to feel inadequate.

Perhaps the trick is to take pride in how I engage with something without tying too much pride to how good I am at it.

Concentrate effort. Diversify identity.
